parts.text: Moist air from the Atlantic meets mountains (1)
It is forced to rise and cools (1)
Rain falls on the windward side; the leeward side is drier (rain shadow) (1)

keywords.def: the weight of air pressing down
an area of low pressure bringing cloud, wind and rain
an area of high pressure bringing settled weather
rain caused by air rising over mountains
a large body of air with similar temperature and moisture

questions.q: Why is western Britain wetter than eastern Britain? (2 marks)
questions.a: Prevailing winds bring moist air from the Atlantic (1); it rises over western hills, giving relief rain, leaving the east in a rain shadow (1)

questions.q: Core: Draw and annotate diagrams of all three types of rain.
Extend: Use your weather diary: was there a day with high pressure? How did the weather match?
Stretch: Explain why convectional rain is common in summer afternoons.
questions.a: The ground heats most in the afternoon, so air rises strongly
B) Settled, dry weather. Sinking air in high pressure stops clouds forming.

questions.q: Big question: why more rain in the Lake District than London?
questions.a: Moist westerly air rises over the Lake District mountains, giving relief rain; London is lower, further east and in a rain shadow
